root_cause: Walkback's ordinary cycle called create_event_ledger.retry_pending_writes, which recursively invoked ensure_schema and executed CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS under the authoritative operations writer lane. The same cycle called anchor reconciliation with an unbounded waiting-row inventory and schema ensures, allowing one transaction to span the historical population. Live owner metadata captured the recurring DDL and self-owned holds over the UI stall threshold.

repair.runtime_ddl: Recurring Walkback calls explicitly use schema-current mode. Read-only startup validators cover the anchor-reconciliation and create-ledger contracts. Standalone/default callers retain existing ensure-schema behavior.
repair.writer_scope: Recurring anchor reconciliation is deterministically limited to the 25 oldest waiting rows per cycle rather than all retained rows.
repair.unchanged: Queue ordering within the selected cohort, retry semantics, attribution, provider behavior, SQLite settings, WAL behavior, timeouts, and other services are unchanged.

new_proofs: recurring retry path cannot call ensure_schema
recurring anchor path cannot call either schema ensure
recurring anchor inventory selects exactly the 25 oldest rows

deployment_scope.observation: Verify zero recurring CREATE statements from Walkback, bounded writer holds, natural Walkback/Cascade progress, and no new SQLite lock failures before resetting the four-hour stabilization clock.
